conviction_note: Near non-result: no company-level number the market lacks was found; three small peer/macro proxies lean negative (mortgage volumes and warehouse balances down in Q3, peer deposit costs and NCOs up), offset by a Fed hike that matched WAL's own NII-guide assumption and short interest that nearly tripled since April; p_up 49 on abs_move 6.0 gives -0.12, and impact_sum -0.4 agrees in sign and is similarly small.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS about $2.44-2.49 (Yahoo 2.44 avg of 13 analysts, range 2.18-2.71; Benzinga 2.43/2.46; Earnings Whispers 2.49) and revenue about $992-994m (Benzinga $992.5m, Earnings Whispers ~$994m). Sources: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/WAL/analysis , https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WAL/earnings-forecasts , https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/WAL (as summarised by search, 2026-10-19). Company guide (Q2 deck slide 17, 2026-07-21): FY26 NII +12-14% on $2.86bn assuming a 25bp September hike, non-interest income +13-17%, deposit costs $650-700m, NCOs 25-35bp, loans +$5bn, deposits +$6bn, CET1 ~11%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026049001/walq22026earningspresent.htm . The revenue consensus (~$993m) sits on the guide's implied H2 run rate, so the bar is the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 6,219,780 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (up from 5,974,409; low 2,251,017 on 2026-04-15), about 5.7% of shares outstanding, 4.73 days to cover (equibles, page read 2026-10-19: https://equibles.com/stocks/wal/shortinterest). Elevated and rising, not crowded. Baseline: 25d skew +5.3 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 2.02 on a thin 2,216 total OI, ATM IV 40.1% against 23% 20d realised, event-implied move 7.68% against a 3.24% median of seven prior reactions (5 of 7 up). Run-up -5.9% over 20d, -0.9% over 5d, -23% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Q3 mortgage conditions worsened against WAL's own baseline: the Freddie Mac 30-year rate went from ~6.49% (2026-06-25) to 6.95-7.03% by mid/late September, and First Horizon, the first warehouse peer to report, said period-end loans to mortgage companies fell $891m (-19%) QoQ to $3,869m; WAL's Q2 call set mortgage banking revenue for Q3 and Q4 at 'about Q2 levels' as a baseline (Q2 gain on sale $53.4m, net servicing $31.3m), so the risk is a shortfall on that line, on period-end C&I loan growth (guided $1.2-1.3bn a quarter) and on the Q4 non-interest income view, partly offset because lower warehouse balances also cut ECR deposit costs in non-interest expense.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21) WAL cut its non-interest income guide from +20-25% to +13-17% on mortgage headwinds and lowered loan growth by $1bn, and the stock still rose 3.61% next session (baseline). The market has not punished mortgage-line cuts on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue (~$993m) is essentially Q2's $995.7m, i.e. it carries management's 'flat mortgage' baseline. If the market had marked mortgage volumes to the higher-rate quarter, estimates would sit below the guide-implied run rate rather than on it; they do not.
findings.independence: Mortgage rates from a separate source: Freddie Mac PMMS 6.49% on 2026-06-25 (https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-average-649) and 7.03% for 2026-09-24 (https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/node/32031/pdf). WAL's own baseline statement: Q2 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/WAL/Q22026). Proxy, not confirmed by WAL; WAL said on that call its warehouse credit needs were already falling, so part of this is in its guide.

findings.finding: Peers that reported Q3 show interest-bearing deposit costs rising before the hike reached them: M&T's cost of interest-bearing deposits went from 1.95% to 2.05% and its NIM from 3.70% to 3.65% QoQ, and First Horizon's interest-bearing deposit costs rose 12bp to 2.45%; WAL guided deposit costs down in Q3 and Q4 through its optimisation programme (about $1bn of high-cost deposits out early Q3 and $750m more by end Q3) and NIM 'stable', against Q2 interest-bearing cost of 2.74%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean record on this line: Q2's NIM of 3.53% (3.54% in Q1) was flat and the stock rose 3.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: WAL's consensus NII must rise about 3-4% QoQ to meet the guide midpoint, which assumes the funding mix improves; rising peer deposit costs would make analysts trim that path, and no WAL-specific revision appeared in what was searched. This is weak, because WAL's cost reduction is a company-specific remixing that peers are not doing.
findings.independence: First Horizon Q3 release, a different issuer (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000178/a3q2026earningsrelease.htm); it shares its document with finding 1. Proxy only. WAL's own Q2 call said its costs were 'trending down 1 to 2 bps exiting June', which cuts against this, so the finding is sized small.

findings.finding: Credit: WAL guided that charge-offs peaked in Q1-Q2, that NPLs fall in H2, and that four of six targeted asset resolutions close by end Q3 (one may slip to Q4), with H2 NCOs a little above the midpoint of 25-35bp; peer M&T's NCOs rose from $80m (0.23%) to $127m (0.35%) with nonaccruals up 7%, and the 7.68% implied move against a 3.24% history median shows the options market is paying for a credit surprise of the October 2025 or March 2026 kind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit disclosures move this name hard: -10.8% on 2025-10-16 (Cantor Group V fraud suit) and roughly -12% pre-market in March 2026 (Jefferies/Leucadia $126.4m charge-off), both outside earnings; Q1 2026 had the LAM charge-off.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the event-implied move is 2.4x the name's own median reaction and the skew pays for downside. What remains unpriced is only whether the resolutions landed on schedule, which is visible at the print. No new WAL-specific credit event was found for Q3.
findings.independence: M&T Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036270/000003627026000057/ex991release3q26.htm) points mildly negative; WAL's own guide points mildly positive. This finding nets the two, and the M&T document is shared with finding 2.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 by a 12-0 vote, which is exactly the September hike WAL's raised FY26 NII guide (+12-14%, tracking to the midpoint) assumed; management said it could 'absorb the 25 basis points of increase to the ECR deposit levels' and modelled earnings +0.8% in both ±100bp ramps, so the macro input to the NII guide came in as assumed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 NII guide raise (low end 11% to 12%) came with a +3.61% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because it sits inside the guide. The small residual is that a held or raised NII guide is now more likely than a cut, while the Q4 ECR offset is the debated item.
findings.independence: WAL Q2 deck slide 17 (assumption of a 25bp September hike): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026049001/walq22026earningspresent.htm

findings.finding: Short interest nearly tripled into the print, from 2.25m shares (2026-04-15) to 6.22m (2026-09-30, about 5.7% of shares outstanding, 4.73 days to cover). The stock is 23% below its 52-week high and 5.9% down over 20 days, and puts are bid (skew +5.3, put/call OI 2.02), so a clean credit print gives a moderate short-cover mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of seven prints since 2025-01 rose; the Q2 2026 print rose 3.61% on an EPS roughly in line with consensus ($2.36 against $2.35-2.37).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism and not information. The downside skew and rising shorts show the market positioned for bad credit news, so an uneventful print has asymmetric room up. If shorts had already covered, short interest would have fallen into the print, and it rose.
findings.independence: Baseline skew and put/call OI (sealed file). The sweep row's July figure (about 4.1m shares, 4.7 days to cover) is consistent with the rise.

outside_window.finding: Basel III re-proposal (March 2026; comments closed 2026-06-18) implies about 81bp of incremental CET1 for WAL per its Q2 call, which management said could fund buybacks into 2027; no final rule was found as of 2026-10-19, so any buyback upsizing on it is after the window unless management pre-announces it on the call.
Crossing $100bn of assets (total assets $98.7bn at Q2) moves WAL into the next regulatory category, likely in 2027; management said it already absorbs about $25m a year of LFI preparation cost.

baseline_tension: The small negative proxies agree with the +5.3 downside skew and the -5.9% 20-day slide, so they are probably priced; the short build and five-of-seven up history cut the other way, which is why p_up sits at 49 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): the mortgage/warehouse finding shrank from -0.6 to -0.5, because lower warehouse balances also cut ECR deposit costs and mortgage banking is about a tenth of revenue
Rule 5 (proxy small, the company's own document beats it): the peer deposit-cost finding shrank from -0.4 to -0.3, since WAL's own call says its costs were trending down on a company-specific remix
Rules 3/5 on p_up: proxy-based lean moved p_up from 48 to 49; abs_move_pct left at 6.0
Rule 6 (bar): three estimate sources agree within $0.06 and sit on the company guide, so there is no cap; left standing
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest of 5.7% is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk on squeeze grounds; the positioning finding was left at +0.4
